title: Substance use disorders and withdrawal syndromes

steps.tx: **Substance use disorder** is recurrent use despite harm with craving, tolerance and loss of control, affecting about ten% to fifteen% of adult patients in surgical and medical wards. India reports **alcohol dependence** in ten% of men and **tobacco use** in thirty five% of adults, with complications across liver, brain and lungs defining chronic **withdrawal syndromes** risk.
steps.say: Substance use disorder is recurrent use despite harm, with craving, tolerance and loss of control. It affects about ten to fifteen percent of adult patients in surgical and medical wards. India reports alcohol dependence in ten percent of men and tobacco use in thirty five percent of adults, with liver, brain and lung complications defining withdrawal risk.

steps.tx: Causes combine **genetic vulnerability**, childhood adversity, early age onset and psychiatric illness with social supply and stress. Peer pressure, cheap alcohol, **child labour** and availability raise risk two to three times, while **depression**, anxiety and schizophrenia double the chance of polysubstance use and relapse within **thirty days** of discharge.
steps.say: Causes combine genetic vulnerability, childhood adversity, early age onset and psychiatric illness with social supply and stress. Peer pressure, cheap alcohol, child work and easy availability raise risk two to three times, while depression, anxiety and schizophrenia double the chance of relapse within thirty days of discharge.

steps.tx: Who uses what and how often matters for withdrawal prediction. This table groups common substances with **prevalence**, primary withdrawal danger and first screening tool, since trainees repeatedly confuse **alcohol delirium tremens** with opioid withdrawal and miss tobacco relapse in hospital. Wards admit **ten% to fifteen%** with alcohol dependence, and **thirty five%** smoke daily, so screening must cover both in **twenty four hours**.
steps.say: Who uses what and how often can help predict withdrawal. This table groups common substances with prevalence, main withdrawal danger and first screening tool. Trainees can repeatedly confuse alcohol delirium tremens with opioid withdrawal and miss tobacco relapse in hospital.

steps.tx: Dependence physiology follows **receptor adaptation** with down regulated GABA and up regulated glutamate. A flow shows chronic suppression, sudden stop, then **autonomic hyperactivity** with seizures and death, which is why **benzodiazepines** protect the brain while fluids alone do not prevent delirium tremens after **seventy two hours**.
steps.say: Dependence physiology follows receptor adaptation, with reduced gamma amino butyric and increased glutamate action. This flow explains chronic suppression, sudden stop, then overactive autonomic nervous activity with seizures and death. Benzodiazepines protect the brain while fluids alone do not prevent delirium tremens after seventy two hours.

steps.tx: **Alcohol withdrawal** starts at six to twelve hours with tremor, anxiety and **autonomic instability**, then seizures at twelve to forty eight hours and **delirium tremens** at forty eight to seventy two hours with hallucinations, fever and **fifteen% mortality**. **CIWA Ar scale** scores guide dosing, while **opioid withdrawal** brings diarrhoea, mydriasis and five to ten days of misery rarely fatal alone.
steps.say: Alcohol withdrawal starts at six to twelve hours with tremor, anxiety and unstable vital signs, then seizures at twelve to forty eight hours and delirium tremens at forty eight to seventy two hours with hallucinations and fever. The CIWA Ar scale guides dosing, while opioid withdrawal brings diarrhoea and wide pupils for many days and is rarely fatal alone.

steps.tx: Two withdrawals are compared directly. This contrast stops the common error of treating **opioid craving** like alcohol delirium, since **seizure risk** and lethal course belong to alcohol and **benzodiazepine** withdrawal, not to opioid syndrome. Trials show combined counselling with **drug assisted detox** cuts relapse to twenty% at six months when family support, follow up and craving management continue together daily.

steps.tx: Screen with **AUDIT C** for alcohol, **Fagerstrom** for nicotine and **COWS** for opioids, then check **full blood count**, **liver function**, **serum a salt balance treatment** and **ECG** before detox. **Gold standard** remains structured history of amount, duration, last use and past withdrawal seizures, because collateral history from family confirms **forty drinks** weekly thresholds better than denial.
steps.say: Screen with AUDIT C for alcohol, Fagerstrom for nicotine and COWS for opioids, then check full blood count, liver function, a salt balance treatment and ECG before detox. The structured history of amount, duration and last use is the reference standard, because family collateral confirms heavy weekly thresholds better than denial.

steps.tx: First line is **symptom triggered chlordiazepoxide** twenty five mg hourly titrated to CIWA below eight, with **a vitamin** one hundred mg before glucose and **magnesium** four g for a salt balance treatment. Give **a sedative** two mg for hepatic dysfunction, **nicotine patch** twenty one mg for smokers and **buprenorphine** four mg for opioid cravings, admitting **delirium tremens** to monitored beds.
steps.say: First line is symptom triggered chlordiazepoxide, twenty five milligrams hourly titrated to CIWA below eight, with a vitamin one hundred milligrams before glucose. Give a sedative for liver disease, nicotine patch twenty one milligrams for smokers and buprenorphine four milligrams for opioid cravings, admitting delirium tremens to monitored beds.

steps.tx: Maintenance uses **naltrexone** fifty mg daily for alcohol opioid abstinence, **acamprosate** six hundred sixty six mg thrice daily for craving, and **a medication that causes severe reaction with alcohol** two hundred fifty mg only with informed consent. **Methadone** forty mg substitution plus **varenicline** one mg for nicotine improves **relapse free** survival at six months, while counselling, **family therapy** and follow up visits decide long term control.
steps.say: Maintenance uses naltrexone fifty milligrams daily for alcohol and opioid abstinence, acamprosate six hundred sixty six milligrams thrice daily for craving, and a medication that causes severe reaction with alcohol only with informed consent. Methadone substitution and varenicline one milligram improve relapse free survival at six months, while counselling and family therapy decide long term control.

steps.tx: Complications include **Wernicke encephalopathy** with ophthalmoplegia, ataxia and confusion, **aspiration** pneumonia, **hepatic failure** and **rhabdomyolysis** in delirium, plus homelessness and **blood borne infections** in injecting users. Prognosis needs **five year follow up**, since relapse exceeds sixty% in first year and rises with untreated **depression** and job loss.
steps.say: Complications include Wernicke encephalopathy with eye palsies, unsteadiness and confusion, breathing infection, liver failure and muscle breakdown in delirium, plus homelessness and blood borne infections in injecting users. Prognosis needs five year follow up, since relapse exceeds sixty percent in the first year and rises with untreated depression.

steps.tx: **High-yield for the exam**: separate alcohol delirium from opioid misery, always give **a vitamin** before glucose, score CIWA before dosing, and never stop **benzodiazepines** abruptly.
